authority: user visual review of the separately loaded Wulong GLB
observations: The lower part of the wall has a prominent stone masonry zone rather than a thin decorative strip.
The upper wall reads as discrete earthen bricks with serious surface weathering.
Surviving plaster remains over parts of the earthen-brick wall.
The wall is generally straight and globally intact; local damage is limited and should not be exaggerated into collapse.
Visible structural timber pieces are embedded in or associated with the wall.
At the door opening, a horizontal timber board or lintel passes into the wall piers.
The wall above the door opening remains continuous with the surrounding wall.
implementationConsequences: Generate a real lower stone masonry assembly with individual stones, mortar joints, adjustable height and slight projection.
Generate upper earthen-brick courses as discrete units with running bond, adjustable brick dimensions and joints.
Treat plaster as a thin overlay with coherent loss areas that reveal the brick courses underneath.
Keep the wall profile nearly vertical and limit geometric damage while allowing heavy surface weathering.
Generate a true door void, an embedded timber lintel that extends into both piers, and continuous masonry above the lintel.

supported: surviving plaster over the brick substrate
unresolved: earthen-brick length, height, depth and mortar composition
timber lintel section, species, count and embed depth
identity of other embedded timber members
